decision.applicability_reason: DelDOT bid package governed by Section 102.8 proposal-guaranty requirements.
decision.explanation: The governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) states the bid security must be 'in an acceptable form and total one-tenth (10%) of the bid amount.' One-tenth (10%) of the bid amount is mathematically identical to 10% of the total bid price. The requirement for acceptable form is also preserved. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause fully satisfies the Challenge Reference Rule. No material deviation exists.
decision.recommended_action: No action required — the proposal guaranty clause in Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf complies with the 10% requirement. Confirm at bid opening that the submitted security instrument is in an acceptable form and equals 10% of the submitted bid price.

criteria.challenge_reference_rule: Where applicable, proposal guaranty must equal 10% of total bid price.

This carries the requirement forward: it mandates that the certification be completed and included with the proposal, which is substantively equivalent to the reference requirement. The capitalization difference ('NON-COLLUSION' vs. 'non-collusive') is a harmless formatting variation expressly excluded from being a deviation by the Challenge Reference Rule. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause is compliant.
decision.recommended_action: No action required. Confirm at bid opening that the signed non-collusive bidding certification form is physically present in the submitted proposal package, as the clause mandates its inclusion.

decision.applicability_reason: Contract execution package governed by Section 103.5 bond requirements.
decision.explanation: Addendum_A.pdf explicitly revises the Performance and Payment Bonds provision and governs over the earlier General_Conditions.pdf text (which stated 75% coverage). The Addendum replacement text at lines Addendum_A.pdf|p1|L7–L8 states bond coverage shall equal 100% of the contract price, subject to the referenced surety conditions — exactly matching the Challenge Reference Rule. decision.applicability_reason: Successful-bidder execution package governed by Section 103.7.
decision.explanation: The governing clause in General_Conditions.pdf (the highest-precedence document addressing this provision) states that the successful bidder shall return required execution documents 'within the reference period' and 'furnish required proof of insurance.' Under the decisional rules, a clause that defers to the reference period rather than restating a specific number is compliant — it incorporates the 20-calendar-day deadline by reference and contradicts nothing. Similarly, 'furnish required proof of insurance' preserves the obligation to provide proof/certificate of insurance before contract execution without negating or altering it. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause is consistent with the Challenge Reference Rule and constitutes no material deviation.
decision.recommended_action: No action required on this provision. Human reviewer may confirm that the phrase 'reference period' is understood by all parties to mean 20 calendar days after notice of award as specified in DelDOT 103.7, but no contractual deviation is present.

decision.applicability_reason: Delaware construction/maintenance contractor context described by the proposal.
decision.explanation: The governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) explicitly states that registration 'must be in place before covered field operations commence.' This directly satisfies the Challenge Reference Rule, which prohibits allowing registration to occur only after work begins. The clause does not permit post-commencement registration; it mandates pre-commencement registration. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause is fully compliant with the reference rule.
decision.recommended_action: No action required — the Contractor Registration Act notice clause in Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf satisfies the reference requirement. Human reviewer may confirm no other package text contradicts this provision.

decision.applicability_reason: Delaware public works proposal subject to 29 Del. C. 6967 licensing.
decision.explanation: Addendum_A.pdf explicitly revises the 'Delaware business / subcontractor licenses' provision and governs over the earlier Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf text (lines L21-L22), which conflicted with the reference by stating bidder license evidence is not required with the proposal and allowing 60 days for subcontractor licenses. The Addendum replacement text at lines L11-L12 defers entirely to 'the reference timing stated in the applicable contract documents,' which is a compliant incorporation-by-reference formulation. It does not contradict any figure, deadline, or obligation in the Challenge Reference Rule — it preserves all obligations by pointing back to the governing reference rather than restating or altering them. Per the operating rules, a clause that defers to the reference rather than repeating its figures is compliant. The superseded earlier text is not a finding. The Addendum corrects the earlier provision.
decision.recommended_action: No action required on this provision. Confirm that the executed contract package includes Addendum_A.pdf and that bidders/contractors are directed to the applicable contract documents for the specific timing requirements under 29 Del. C. § 6967. Human reviewer should verify the superseded Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf text is clearly displaced by the Addendum in the final executed package.

decision.explanation: The governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) explicitly states that 'later issued Addenda may be disregarded.' This directly contradicts the Challenge Reference Rule, which requires the package to acknowledge current addenda and prohibits treating the original proposal as self-updating. Project metadata confirms Addendum 1 was issued. No Addendum in the package revises this specific provision — Addendum_A.pdf addresses bonds and licenses only, leaving the defective addenda-acknowledgment clause operative. The clause affirmatively negates the requirement by making acknowledgment of later-issued addenda optional ('may be disregarded'), which is a material deviation.
decision.recommended_action: Human review required. The addenda acknowledgment clause in Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf expressly permits bidders to disregard later-issued addenda, including the project's own Addendum 1. This clause should be corrected to require acknowledgment of all issued addenda before the package is used or executed.

decision.applicability_reason: Multiple contract documents are incorporated and may conflict, so DelDOT 105.6 applies.
decision.explanation: The governing clause in General_Conditions.pdf (the highest-ranked document for this provision) instructs that all contract documents be read together and that conflicts be resolved by applying 'the same priority sequence listed in the applicable contract documents.' This is a compliant incorporation-by-reference formulation: it preserves both the complementary-treatment obligation and the conflict-resolution obligation by deferring to the priority sequence in the applicable contract documents rather than restating the full hierarchy. Under the operating rules, a clause that defers to the reference rather than repeating its figures or sequence is NOT a deviation. No Addendum revises this provision. The clause does not negate, narrow, or contradict any element of DelDOT 105.6. Accordingly, no material deviation exists.
decision.recommended_action: No action required. Confirm that the phrase 'the same priority sequence listed in the applicable contract documents' is understood by project staff to refer to the DelDOT 105.6 hierarchy; no substantive change is needed.

criteria.challenge_reference_rule: Treat contract documents as complementary and resolve conflicts using DelDOT 105.6. decision.applicability_reason: Package includes change-notification requirements under DelDOT 104.3.
decision.explanation: The governing document (General_Conditions.pdf) addresses change notification at lines L17–L19. The clause states that 'alleged changes require timely written notice and the reference follow-up documentation within the stated period.' This language defers to the reference rather than restating specific figures: 'timely written notice' carries forward the immediacy requirement, and 'within the stated period' defers to the 7-calendar-day deadline in the governing reference rather than contradicting it. Under the operating rules, a clause that defers to the reference instead of repeating its numbers is compliant — a missing number is not an omission when the clause defers to the reference and contradicts nothing. The clause does not negate, shorten, or make optional any element of the reference rule. No Addendum revises this provision. Accordingly, no material deviation is present.
decision.recommended_action: Review and confirm that the deferred 'stated period' is understood by all parties to mean the 7-calendar-day deadline in DelDOT 104.3, and that 'timely written notice' is understood to encompass the immediate oral-and-written notice requirement. No legal conclusion is made.

decision.applicability_reason: Contract and subcontract performance records are subject to the Right to Audit notice.
decision.explanation: The package text deviates from the reference in two material respects. First, it limits audit scope to 'only prime-contractor records,' expressly excluding subcontractor records, whereas the reference requires both prime-contractor and subcontractor records to be available for audit. Second, it shortens the retention period from three years (as required) to one (1) year after final payment. Both are affirmative conflicts with specific figures and scope obligations stated in the reference. No Addendum revises this provision, and the governing document (Proposal_and_General_Notices.pdf) carries this defective text. Human review is recommended to correct both the scope limitation and the retention period.
decision.recommended_action: Review and correct the Right to Audit clause to (1) extend audit scope to include subcontractor records and (2) restore the retention period to three years after final payment, consistent with the reference requirement.

decision.applicability_reason: Package includes a liquidated-damages provision or governing schedule.
decision.explanation: The Special Provisions clause at the governing document explicitly states that 'the governing contract/reference schedule shall be used' and affirmatively negates any universal flat rate by stating 'no single invented flat rate applies to all contract values.' This is fully consistent with the Challenge Reference Rule, which requires rate logic tied to the applicable reference schedule and prohibits a universal invented flat daily rate. The clause defers to the reference schedule rather than substituting an arbitrary figure, which is compliant under the operating rules. No Addendum revises this provision. No material deviation exists.
decision.recommended_action: No action required — confirm that the project's executed contract documents incorporate the DelDOT 108.9 schedule by reference and that no separate exhibit introduces a flat daily rate.

criteria.challenge_reference_rule: Use the governing Section 108.9 liquidated-damages schedule/rate logic for the applicable contract value and time basis after resolving Addenda and precedence. A universal invented flat daily rate is a material deviation.
criteria.review_expectation: Verify liquidated-damages rate logic is tied to the applicable reference schedule rather than an unsupported arbitrary amount.
